battle.name: 唐擊焉耆之戰
battle.brief: 貞觀十八年（644）秋，唐太宗以侯君集為交河道行軍大總管，率兵與西域諸國兵西征塔里木盆地東南緣的焉耆國。大軍出玉門、越蔥嶺，直抵孔雀河上游的都城員渠城，牛進達為先鋒破城，擒焉耆王龍突茲送京師。卡面的埃及長矛早此四千餘年，是青銅矛的祖型，與唐軍步槊、長矛同出一脈。

kit.name: 埃及長矛
kit.history: 早王朝時期的長矛，銅或青銅矛頭綁在木杆上。埃及人用它守城垣，後來也用它收復失地。

countries: 貞觀十八年（644）唐擊焉耆之戰，交戰的兩方，一邊是唐王朝及其在西域的盟國與從軍部落，另一邊是塔里木盆地東南緣的綠洲王國焉耆。焉耆是西域七國之一，都城員渠城在今新疆焉耆回族自治縣一帶，位於孔雀河（開都河）上游，其國力全靠城郭與灌溉渠系的綠洲。牠與西面的龜茲國（都庫車城）世代相鄰，兩國在水源、綠洲與商道上積怨，貞觀十七、十八年間互相攻掠，龜茲王於是派使入唐控訴，把糾紛送上唐廷。焉耆一方並非孤立的城邦：其王龍突茲一面遣使入朝貢奉，一面與西突厥往來，又向臣於突厥的吐谷渾方向求援，企圖以域外大國的干預對抗唐兵。唐一方投入的是帝國式的遠征：以侯君集為交河道行軍大總管，統一指揮河西防區與安西都護府系統的兵將，以及西域諸國提供的從軍兵與夫役；軍隊分若干軍府與行軍總管府編制，糧秣由涼州、瓜州一線轉輸，沿途設驛、置屯田。指揮體系的特徵是兵將分離而號令統一：大軍由尚書省與兵部調發，總管府設判官、書記隨軍處理軍令文書，軍糧由度支核給，而遠在長安的皇帝以詔書與飛符掌握分寸，戰況與糧況可逐日傳達。
countriesEn: The Tang campaign against Yanqi of 644 was fought between the Tang dynasty, acting through its client states in the Western Regions, and the oasis kingdom of Yanqi on the south-eastern rim of the Tarim basin. Yanqi was one of the seven states of the Western Regions; its capital was Yuanqu city, in the neighbourhood of what is now Yarkand county in Xinjiang, on the upper reaches of the Peacock River, and the whole strength of the state rested on the town and on the irrigated oasis worked by its channels. It bordered Kucha to the west, whose capital was the city of Kuqa, and the two states were long neighbours and old rivals over water, over oasis land and over the trade roads. Between the seventeenth and eighteenth years of Zhenguan they raided each other, and the king of Kucha sent an envoy to the Tang court to complain, and so carried the quarrel to the throne. Yanqi was not an isolated city-state. Its king, Longtuzi, sent embassies to court with tribute while at the same time keeping up relations with the Western Turks, and he looked for support in the direction of the Tuyuhun, who were then subject to the Turks, in the hope of bringing the weight of the powers beyond the passes to bear against a Tang army. The Tang side committed an expedition organised on an imperial scale. Hou Junji was appointed Grand Chief of the March to the River Course, and under him were the officers and men of the Hexi defence line and of the Anxi Protectorate system, together with the troops and the service men supplied by the states of the Western Regions. The host was divided into a number of military offices and travelling headquarters, the grain was carried forward from the line of Liangzhou and Guazhou, and relay stations and tuntian fields were established along the road. The command system was marked by the separation of soldiers from commanders and by the unity of the orders: the host was mustered by the Department of State Affairs and the Ministry of War, the headquarters carried judges and record-keepers to handle the written business of the army, the rations were drawn against the accounts of the Revenue and Finance departments, and the emperor, far away in Chang'an, kept his hand on the measure of things by edict and by flying dispatch, so that the state of the fighting and of the supply could be reported day by day.
people: 留在這場戰役記錄裡的人，大致可分四類。第一類是唐廷的決策者：太宗李世民是遠征的發動者。貞觀十八年，他收到龜茲王的控訴與譯經僧辯機的報告，知道焉耆王不聽詔命，又察覺焉耆與西突厥的往來，最後決定用兵，而不是像前代那樣只遣使責問；他不親征，而以侯君集統軍。第二類是唐軍的將領：侯君集是唐初最善於西域戰事的主將，此前已於貞觀十四年平高昌，此次再出塔里木，是唐軍第二次大規模西征；他在軍中持重而敢進，對朝中「深入則有萬一之險」的顧慮，他以兵可輕而糧道可支的理由力主進取。副總管牛進達素以勇力著稱，據舊唐書所載，他在焉耆攻城時為先鋒，率先登城，破了這座孔雀河畔的都城。第三類是兩國的君主：焉耆王龍突茲在唐初曾多次遣使入朝，最終在城破之日被擒，押送長安後獲赦，授右武衛大將軍；龜茲王白相（一作玷）是這場戰爭的報怨者，他向唐廷控訴焉耆而獲暫時的信任，貞觀二十二年龜茲再叛時他被廢。第四類是僧人與周邊人物：譯經僧辯機以使者的身分出使焉耆責問，回國後力陳焉耆抗命，成為開戰的直接導火之一；他其後因另一件涉及金寶的案件在貞觀二十三年被處死，而當時玄奘尚在印度求法，焉耆正是他西行路上第一個停留的綠洲大國，高昌王麴文泰阻斷商旅、西突厥控制綠洲北緣，則是這場遠征背後更大的棋局。
peopleEn: The people whose names remain attached to this campaign fall into four groups. The first are the decision-makers at the Tang court. Taizong, Li Shimin, was the man who set the expedition in motion. In the eighteenth year of Zhenguan, 644, he received the complaint of the king of Kucha and the report of the translator-monk Bianji, learned that the king of Yanqi would not obey the imperial summons, and detected the traffic between Yanqi and the Western Turks; he then decided on force rather than sending yet another embassy to remonstrate, and he did not campaign in person but gave the command to Hou Junji. The second group are the Tang commanders. Hou Junji was among the most capable of the Tang commanders in western campaigning, having already taken Gaochang in the fourteenth year of Zhenguan, and this was the second great Tang expedition into the Tarim basin. He was careful in the camp and bold in the attack, and against the objection often voiced at court, that a deep advance risks everything, he argued that the force was light and that the line of supply could be sustained, and pressed for the advance. His deputy, Niu Jinda, was noted for his strength, and the Jiu Tangshu has it that he led the vanguard in the assault on Yanqi and was the first over the wall, and that he took the city on the banks of the Peacock River. The third group are the two kings. Longtuzi of Yanqi had sent embassies to the Tang court several times in the early years of the reign; in the end he was taken prisoner on the day the city fell, was carried to the capital, was pardoned, and was made commander of the Right Martial Guard. Bai Xiang, also written Zhan, king of Kucha, was the man who brought the quarrel to Tang in the first place: he complained of Yanqi to the court and enjoyed a measure of the court's trust, and when Kucha rebelled again four years later he was put aside. The fourth group are the monks and the neighbouring actors. The translator-monk Bianji was sent as envoy to Yanqi to put the question, and on his return he insisted that Yanqi had defied the imperial command, which was one of the immediate sparks of the war; he was later put to death in the twenty-third year of Zhenguan on an unrelated charge concerning treasure. At that time Xuanzang was still in India, and Yanqi was the first great oasis in which he had stayed on his journey west. The king of Gaochang, Qu Wentai, who cut the trade routes, and the Western Turks, who held the northern rim of the oases, formed the larger board on which this campaign was played.
kits: 卡面這件埃及長矛（Egyptian spear）不曾出現在焉耆的城牆上：它是早王朝時期的器物，約公元前3200年前後成形，銅或青銅矛頭安在木杆上，靠纏束固定，用於守城垣與近身刺擊，埃及人靠它收復失地。把它放進貞觀十八年的裝備表，理由是它代表長杆矛這一技術路線的源頭，而唐軍在焉耆城下的長杆兵器，正是同一條路線在東亞的成熟形態。公元七世紀中葉的唐軍裝備可分五層說。第一層是刺擊：步槊與長矛，槊杆長於槍，槊刃窄長如鳥喙，專供騎兵使用；步兵的矛沿用隋制，矛頭與柲分作兩截，以皮條與漆麻纏合，銅鐵兼用，與埃及矛頭綁在木杆上的做法並無二致，只是工藝更細。第二層是劈砍：橫刀供騎戰，陌刀是雙手長刀，刀身狹長直刃，帶有西域樣式，供步戰破陣；另有方天戟、錘、鎗。第三層是防護：明光甲是胸前綴金屬護片的札甲，玄甲是通漆黑色的具裝人馬，另有頓盾、拒馬槊與鹿角。第四層是遠射與攻城：唐弩是臂長數尺的擘張弩，用來壓制城頭，弓矢之外有投石機（石砲與木砲），攻城則用巢車、飛雲棚、撞車與雲梯。第五層是後勤：運輸靠驛馬、牛車與人力，軍糧由河西走廊轉輸，行軍與糧道因此成為這場戰爭最大的技術難題。
kitsEn: The Egyptian spear on the card never stood on the walls of Yanqi. It is a piece of the Old Kingdom, formed about 3200 BC, with a copper or bronze head fixed to a wooden shaft by binding, used to defend walls and to stab at close quarters, and the Egyptians recovered lost territory with it. It belongs in the equipment table of 644 because it represents the source of the long-shafted spear, and the long-shafted weapons of the Tang army at the gates of Yanqi are the same line of development at its mature stage in East Asia. The equipment of a Tang army in the middle of the seventh century can be described in five layers. The first is the thrust: the infantry spear and the cavalry lance. The shaft of the lance is longer than that of a spear, and its blade is narrow and long like a bird's beak, made for mounted men; the infantry spear followed the Sui pattern, with the head and the shaft made separately and bound together with thongs of leather and hemp covered in lacquer, in copper or in iron, which is in principle no different from the Egyptian practice of binding a head to a wooden shaft, only finer in the workmanship. The second is the cut: the hengdao for fighting from horseback, and the modao, a two-handed long knife with a narrow straight blade of western Asian appearance, used to break ranks on foot; and also the fangtian halberd, the mace and the trident. The third is protection: the Mingguang armour, a lamellar cuirass with metal plates fixed to the breast, the dark lacquered armour of men and horses, and further the dun shield, the refuse-horse lance and the deer-horn obstacle. The fourth is missile and siege: the Tang crossbow, a powerful bow several feet in the span of its arms, used to dominate the walls; the bow and arrow; and the stone and wooden catapults. For the assault itself the army had the siege tower, the flying cloud shed, the battering ram and the scaling ladder. The fifth is logistics: transport by relay horse, ox cart and human porter, with the grain of the army carried along the Hexi corridor, so that movement and supply remained the hardest technical problem of this campaign.
tactics: 這場戰爭的戰術可以分行軍、攻城、接管三段來看。行軍段是最艱難的一段：自長安出發，經涼州、瓜州，出玉門關，渡流沙，越蔥嶺，穿越天山南麓的雪山與隘口，行程以數千里計，途中缺水少糧，只能靠沿途屯田與西域諸國提供的駱駝、馬匹接濟，因此大軍不能久滯，必須速戰。侯君集抵焉耆後沒有立刻動手攻城，先遣偵探與遊騎查清城防、水源與城內糧儲，並封鎖往龜茲與西突厥方向的通道，斷其外援，孤立守軍，這與唐初對高昌的辦法同出一轍。攻城段由副總管牛進達主持：唐軍以巢車、飛雲棚與雲梯逼近城牆，先以弩與投石機壓制城頭守兵，再由敢死之士攀垣而入，破了位於孔雀河畔的都城員渠城。奪城之後，戰術重心轉為接管：唐軍據城、分路搜捕拒降者、把焉耆國境劃為羈縻性質的安置區、留兵駐守，隨後把安西都護府的管轄線向東推進。防守方的戰術則以城為依托：閉門固守、拖延待援，靠城郭與灌溉水利的守禦優勢撐時間，但因外交上的失誤與求援無果，外援始終沒有到來。
tacticsEn: The tactics of this war can be read in three stages: the march, the assault and the taking over. The march was the hardest of them. From Chang'an the army went by Liangzhou and Guazhou, out through the Yumen Pass, across the shifting sands, over the Congling range, and through the snowy passes of the southern Tian Shan, a distance counted in thousands of li, short of water and short of grain on the way. The host could only be supplied by the tuntian fields along the road and by the camels and horses the states of the Western Regions provided, and it could therefore not linger and had to strike quickly. When Hou Junji reached Yanqi he did not attack at once. He first sent out scouts and mounted patrols to learn the state of the defences, the water and the grain stored inside, and he closed the roads towards Kucha and towards the Western Turks, cutting off outside help and isolating the garrison, which is the same method used against Gaochang in the early Tang. The assault was led by the deputy Niu Jinda: the siege towers, the flying cloud sheds and the scaling ladders were brought up to the wall, the defenders on the crest were first pinned down by the crossbows and the catapults, and then the men who had volunteered for the first ascent went over the wall, and the capital Yuanqu on the banks of the Peacock River was taken. After the city fell the emphasis of the operation shifted to the taking over: the army occupied the town, mounted patrols swept the country for those who refused to surrender, the territory of Yanqi was turned into a zone of jimi settlement, a garrison was left behind, and the line of the Anxi Protectorate was then pushed eastward. The tactics of the defence were built on the town: the gates were shut, the walls held out for time, and the advantage of the walls and of the irrigation works was used to delay. But because help was mismanaged at the diplomatic level and the appeal for aid never came, no relief ever arrived.
data: 可核對的數字分三類。第一類是系年與人名可查的數字：遠征始於貞觀十八年（644），唐太宗以侯君集為交河道行軍大總管，大軍於同年秋發兵西行，至十月破焉耆城、擒龍突茲，是年冬龍突茲已被押抵長安並獲赦，授右武衛大將軍；從出師到擒王，跨越玉門與蔥嶺，路上約兩個月，真正攻城只在數日之間。兵力方面，唐軍本部與西域諸國從軍兵力的總數各史均無確載，常見的概數是萬餘人，加上諸國之兵與夫役，總量當在數萬之譜；焉耆方面是城守之眾，數字更無從核實。距離方面，焉耆城距長安約五千餘里，古代輿圖形容為出玉門數千里，按今里程約三千五百公里以上。第二類是考古與文獻數字：焉耆漢唐城址（員渠城遺址，在今焉耆縣城一帶）經歷年發掘，出土唐代陶製明器、錢幣與大量相關文書；吐魯番交河故城出土的唐代官府公文裡，反覆出現調發焉耆馬匹、糧食與兵員的記錄，說明這場戰爭真正的代價是長期的駐軍與輸送開銷，而吞下來的是一座需要長期供血的綠洲。第三類是推估，必須打折：遠征的實際戰損，各家史書都沒有留下數字，只說士卒疲敝，這類概括無法換算成具體人數。
dataEn: The numbers that can be checked fall into three classes. The first is the chronology and the names, which are documented. The expedition began in the eighteenth year of Zhenguan, 644: Taizong appointed Hou Junji Grand Chief of the March to the River Course, the host set out west in the autumn of that year, in the tenth month the city of Yanqi was taken and Longtuzi was captured, and in the winter of the same year Longtuzi had been carried to the capital and pardoned, being made commander of the Right Martial Guard. From the departure of the army to the capture of the king, two months were spent on the road across Yumen and the Congling range, and the storming of the town itself took only a few days. As for the numbers of troops, neither the Tang host nor the contingents supplied by the states of the Western Regions has any exact figure in the histories; the usual rough statement is some ten thousand men, and with the troops and the service men of the states the total must have run to tens of thousands. On the Yanqi side there was the garrison of the city, and its numbers cannot be checked at all. As for distance, the town of Yanqi lies some five thousand li from Chang'an, the old maps describing the road as several thousand li beyond Yumen, which is a little over three thousand five hundred kilometres by the reckoning of today. The second class is archaeological and documentary. The Han and Tang site of Yanqi, the remains of Yuanqu city in the neighbourhood of the present county town of Yarkand, has been excavated over many years and has yielded Tang pottery, coins and a great deal of related written material; in the official Tang documents from Jiaohe near Turfan there recur records of the requisition of horses, grain and men from Yanqi, which shows that the real cost of this war lay in the long-term garrison and in the transport, and that what was taken on was an oasis that would have to be fed for a long time. The third class is estimate, and must be discounted. No history gives the actual losses of the expedition in figures; the remark that the soldiers were exhausted is not convertible into a number of men.
cause: 打起來的原因有三層，由近及遠。最直接的一層是龜茲與焉耆的邊境糾紛：龜茲王入唐控訴焉耆侵掠，唐朝既在西域居中仲裁，就有義務處置諸國的爭端，於是先遣辯機齎詔責問焉耆，而龍突茲不肯聽命，這件事本身還不足以開戰。第二層是焉耆王的戰略選擇：龍突茲清楚以一國之力不能抵擋唐廷認真出兵，所以一面遣使貢奉以拖延，一面遣使西突厥求援，企圖讓唐軍越過蔥嶺之後遇上突厥騎兵與西域聯軍，把遠征變成消耗戰；唐廷正因為察覺焉耆與西突厥、吐蕃方向的聯繫，才把這場衝突從邊民糾紛提升為國策問題。第三層是唐朝在西域的整體戰略：貞觀十四年平高昌後，唐在高昌一帶設西都護府，切斷了麴氏與西突厥的依托，也切斷了商旅；焉耆、龜茲這些綠洲城國既注定被捲入唐與突厥的對抗，就必須選邊站。對唐太宗而言，出兵焉耆不是為了幾千平方里的綠洲地盤，而是為了讓安西都護府有一個可靠的西鄰，讓唐的聲威與商路能自敦煌一路通到龜茲、疏勒、于闐。
causeEn: There are three layers of reason, from the nearest to the most distant. The nearest is the quarrel between Kucha and Yanqi over their border. The king of Kucha came to the Tang court to accuse Yanqi of raiding, and the Tang, sitting in the middle of the Western Regions as arbiter, had an obligation to settle the disputes of the states; it therefore sent Bianji with an imperial message to rebuke Yanqi, and Longtuzi refused to obey. That in itself would not have been enough to make war. The second layer is the strategic choice of the king of Yanqi. Longtuzi knew that a single state could not withstand a Tang army once the court had decided to be serious, so he sent envoys with tribute to gain time while at the same time appealing to the Western Turks, hoping that after crossing the Congling range the Tang army would meet Turk cavalry and a coalition from the Western Regions, and that a distant expedition would be worn down into a war of attrition. Precisely because the court had detected the connection of Yanqi with the Western Turks and with the Tibetan direction, the clash was raised from a quarrel of border folk to a matter of state policy. The third layer is the overall strategy of the Tang in the Western Regions. After Gaochang was taken in the fourteenth year of Zhenguan, the Tang set up the Western Protectorate in the Gaochang area, cutting the Qu family off from its support in the Western Turks and cutting the trade routes; oasis states such as Yanqi and Kucha, which were bound to be drawn into the contest between the Tang and the Turks, had to pick a side. For Taizong the object of the expedition was not a few thousand square li of oasis land; it was to give the Anxi Protectorate a reliable western neighbour, so that the authority and the trade of the Tang might run unbroken from Dunhuang as far as Kucha, Kashgar and Khotan.
impact: 這場戰爭的影響，在唐史與西域史上都算重要。第一，它打通了安西都護府在塔里木盆地南緣的東段：焉耆既入唐，唐得以在孔雀河上游設官置兵，把安西的防線從高昌、吐魯番一線推到龜茲以東，後來安西四鎮（焉耆、龜茲、疏勒、于闐）的格局，正是從這一步逐步成形；貞觀二十二年（648）侯君集再平龜茲之後，安西都護府自交河移治龜茲，唐在西域的常設機構才真正落戶。第二，它改變了西域城國之間的權力平衡：焉耆被打服之後，龜茲一度獨強，卻在四年後反叛被平，說明一次遠征只能改變一時的服從，維持西域秩序靠的是常駐的軍鎮、屯田與馬匹供給，而不是某一場會戰。第三，它對佛教與西域知識的傳播有間接推力：西行求法的僧侶在焉耆、龜茲停留，得到僧眾與物資的支助，玄奘於貞觀十九年（645）歸國後譯出的經典與西域記，是唐人對西域認識的第一次系統整理，而辯機這位奉命出使的譯經僧恰好橫跨在這兩件事的中間。第四，它留下的經驗被記在兵書與史論裡：遠征西域，糧道決定成敗，必須屯田自給；深入則有萬一之險，須以輕兵疾進與斷其外援配合。這幾條後來成了唐兵書中西征條目的核心。
impactEn: The effects of this campaign matter both in Tang history and in the history of the Western Regions. First, it opened the eastern section of the Anxi Protectorate's line along the southern rim of the Tarim basin. With Yanqi brought in, the Tang could set up officials and station soldiers on the upper Peacock River, pushing the frontier of Anxi from the Gaochang and Turfan line eastward beyond Kucha; the later pattern of the four garrisons of Anxi, at Yanqi, Kucha, Kashgar and Khotan, grew step by step out of this beginning. When Hou Junji took Kucha again in the twenty-second year of Zhenguan, 648, the Anxi Protectorate was moved from Jiaohe to Kucha, and only then did the permanent Tang institution in the west settle down. Second, it altered the balance of power among the oasis states. With Yanqi beaten, Kucha was strong for a time, and yet it rebelled and was put down four years later, which shows that a single expedition can change the submission of the moment only, and that order in the Western Regions was kept by permanent garrisons, by tuntian fields and by the supply of horses, not by any one battle. Third, it gave an indirect push to the spread of Buddhism and to the knowledge of the west. Monks travelling west to seek the dharma stayed at Yanqi and at Kucha and were helped there by the monastic communities with provisions and transport; the scriptures Xuanzang translated and the record of the western regions he wrote after returning in the nineteenth year of Zhenguan, 645, were the first systematic account of the west that the Tang had; and Bianji, the translator-monk sent as envoy, stands exactly between the two undertakings. Fourth, the experience of the campaign was written into the military manuals and into historical judgements: to campaign in the Western Regions the line of supply decides the outcome, and one must grow one's own grain by tuntian; to advance deeply risks everything, and one must combine a light and rapid advance with cutting off the enemy's help. These became the core of the western campaign entries in the Tang military literature.
result: 貞觀十八年（644）秋，侯君集的大軍出玉門、越蔥嶺，抵達孔雀河上游的焉耆都城員渠城，牛進達率先鋒破城，焉耆王龍突茲被擒，隨軍送抵京師；太宗赦其死，授右武衛大將軍，唐朝隨即在焉耆置都督府、派官治理、分兵駐守，龜茲王白相遣使入朝謝罪進貢並請置官屬。從軍事結果看，這是一場乾淨利落的速決：唐軍以數月的遠征取得一座西域重鎮與其綠洲地盤，代價主要體現在後方的糧秣輸送，而不是戰場上的折損；但戰果並不安穩。貞觀二十二年（648）龜茲起兵反唐，侯君集再以昆陵道行軍大總管出征，破龜茲、廢其王，唐乃把安西都護府自交河移治龜茲，才把兩次遠征的成果連成一線。焉耆方面，唐朝並未把它劃入郡縣式的版圖，而是保留國號與王族、令其內附，這是唐對西域城國一貫的羈縻辦法。結果可以這樣概括：唐擊焉耆之戰以一次奔襲完成，證明了帝國遠征在技術上可行，也暴露了它在糧道與羈縻上的弱點；此後西域的秩序，靠的不是某一場勝利，而是十餘年不斷的用兵與經營。
resultEn: In the autumn of 644, Hou Junji's host went out through Yumen, crossed the Congling range and reached the capital of Yanqi, Yuanqu, on the upper Peacock River; Niu Jinda led the vanguard, the city was taken, and the king of Yanqi, Longtuzi, was captured and sent to the capital with the army. Taizong remitted his death and made him commander of the Right Martial Guard, and the Tang at once set up a military commission at Yanqi, appointed officials, and left a garrison; and the king of Kucha, Bai Xiang, sent an envoy to court to apologise, to offer tribute and to ask for the establishment of officials. Judged as a military result, this was a clean and quick decision: in an expedition of some months the Tang army took a strategic town of the Western Regions together with the oasis that belonged to it, and the cost fell mainly on the transport of grain behind the front rather than on losses in the field. Yet the result was not secure. In 648 Kucha rose in revolt against the Tang; Hou Junji marched out again as Grand Chief of the March to the Kunling Road, took Kucha and set its king aside, and the Tang then moved the Anxi Protectorate from Jiaohe to Kucha, and only then were the gains of the two expeditions joined into a single line. In Yanqi itself the Tang did not fold the country into the commanderies of the interior; the name of the state and the line of its king were kept and it was made a dependent member of the empire, which was the jimi arrangement the Tang used consistently with the oasis states of the west. The result can be put this way. The Tang campaign against Yanqi was carried through as a single rush, proving that a distant imperial expedition was technically possible, and at the same time exposing its weakness in supply and in the loose control of client states. The order of the Western Regions after that was not kept by any one victory, but by ten years of continual campaigning and of keeping up the garrisons.
